newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes up against US dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes up against US dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan closed up at 8.2974 against the U.S. dollar on Thursday from Wednesday's 8.2980 on the Shanghai-based interbank foreign exchange market in dull trading, dealers said.
Dealers said most traders had little interest in trading because the yuan had been stuck in a narrow range of 8.2970 and 8.2980 for several days.
The yuan opened up at 8.2974 and consolidated between 8.2972 and 8.2976 for most of the session, hitting an intra-day high of 8.2964 and a low of 8.2977.
Trading was dull, with most done at 8.2974, traders said.

"Some banks continued to sell dollars earned from exports, which pushed the yuan up to its highest level today," one dealer said. "But the yuan was firmly capped at a topside of 8.2970, possibly by central bank intervention," he added.
"Given that prices are too stable, most banks had no intention of trading for their own use," said a second dealer.
Dealers expect the yuan to consolidate at current levels on Friday.
The yuan fell sharply against 100 Japanese yen to close at 7.3700 from 7.2610 due to the yen's rise against the U.S. dollar in the world market.
The yuan ended unchanged at 1.0738 against the Hong Kong dollar.
